title: Open subschemes of a Noetherian affine scheme of dimension at most one
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be its affine scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], and suppose that the topological Krull dimension of $X$ is at most one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Then every open subscheme $U\subseteq X$ is affine, including the empty open.

source.place: Tag 09N9, lemma-open-in-affine-curve-affine (Noetherian affine specialization: opens are quasi-compact)

proof.text: By the affine Noetherian-space lemma, $|X|$ is Noetherian, since $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)=A$. The compact-subsets lemma therefore makes $U$ and every $U\cap V$ quasi-compact, for every open $V\subseteq X$. In particular $U$ is retrocompact and its inclusion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ is quasi-compact: the inverse image of an affine open $V$ is $U\cap V$. The diagonal $U\to U\times_XU$ is an isomorphism, since an open inclusion is a monomorphism. An isomorphism preserves quasi-compactness of opens, so this diagonal is quasi-compact and $j$ is quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 09N9, quasi-compactness hypothesis and the application of Tag 01LC; Algebra Tag 00FQ (lemma-Noetherian-topology), Topology Tag 04ZA (lemma-Noetherian-quasi-compact)

proof.text: For $x=\mathfrak p\in X$, clause (1) of the affine-stalk localization lemma identifies $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ with $A_{\mathfrak p}$. This ring is Noetherian directly from the definition: given an ideal $J\subseteq A_{\mathfrak p}$, let $I=\{a\in A:a/1\in J\}$. Choose finite generators $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ of $I$. For $a/s\in J$, the unit $s/1$ gives $a/1\in J$, so $a\in I$; writing $a=\sum_i b_ia_i$ gives $a/s=\sum_i(b_i/s)(a_i/1)$. Thus $a_i/1$ generate $J$.

source.place: Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), localization argument in the first sentence of proof; applied to the stalks in Tag 09N9

proof.text: The stalk-dimension lemma expresses $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}$ as the supremum of lengths of chains $\overline{\{x\}}=Z_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq Z_n$ of irreducible closed subsets of $X$. Every such chain is among the chains defining $\dim X$. Therefore $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}\leq\dim X\leq1$ for every $x\in X$.

source.place: Tag 02IZ (lemma-codimension-local-ring); comparison of the two chain suprema supplies the local-dimension hypothesis of Tag 09N9

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-module $\mathcal F$. The retrocompactness established in Step 1 and the local-ring conclusions of Steps 2 and 3 verify every hypothesis of the retrocompact-open higher-direct-image vanishing lemma. Applying it gives $R^qj_*\mathcal F=0$ for every $q>0$.

source.place: Tag 09N9, first application in its proof: Tag 09N8 (lemma-affine)

proof.text: Since j is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, its pushforward G = j_* F is quasi-coherent. Apply the source library affine-scheme cohomology vanishing directly to G on X, obtaining H^1(X,G)=0 in the Ext model Scheme.Modules.H. This is the same affine-vanishing step of Stacks 09N9; it avoids the intermediate openModuleCohomology model.

source.place: Tag 09N9, the applications of Schemes Tag 01LC (lemma-push-forward-quasi-coherent) and Cohomology of Schemes Tag 01XB (lemma-quasi-coherent-affine-cohomology-zero)

proof.text: Apply the acyclic-pushforward linear Leray comparison with p=j, f=id_X and coefficient F. The higher-direct-image vanishing from Step 4 supplies the hypothesis. In degree one this gives an equivalence H^1(X,j_* F) ≃ H^1(U,F), so Step 5 makes H^1(U,F) a subsingleton.

source.place: Tag 01F4 (lemma-apply-Leray), part (1), exactly as used in Tag 09N9

proof.text: Take F to be each quasi-coherent ideal I on U. The module-cohomology source comparison is an additive equivalence from module right-derived sections to Scheme.Modules.H; its injectivity transfers the subsingleton conclusion of Step 6 to module cohomology. Since U is quasi-compact by Step 1, apply the quasi-compact H^1 affineness criterion. None of these steps assumes U is nonempty.

source.place: Tag 01XF (lemma-quasi-compact-h1-zero-covering), used at the end of Tag 09N9

proof_origin.place: Tag 09N9, lemma-open-in-affine-curve-affine; the Lean proof uses the source H model for affine vanishing and Leray, then the existing module-cohomology comparison for Serre’s criterion
